observations: Photo 0: front panel of an office photocopier wrapped in clear stretch film; badge reads 'SHARP AR-M207' clearly.
Photo 1: side and front of what looks like the same copier on a wooden pallet, 'SHARP' badge partly legible, 'digital' logo, Energy Star sticker, two paper cassettes marked A4 and A3.
Photo 2: top and front of a copier under film with the platen cover, a wooden board strapped on top, 'SHARP AR-M207' badge visible.
Casing is off-white with yellowing and scuffs under the film; no visible cracks.
Watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI SMATECH MEGA EQUIPMENT' on every photo, a dealer stock watermark.
No photo shows the unit powered on, the control panel display, a test copy, or the page counter.
Only the outside is shown: drum, fuser, toner and cassettes interiors are not shown.

claims.evidence: Origin cannot be shown by photos; the film wrap suggests imported stock but proves nothing.

claims.claim: The AR-M207 with an extensive range of functions
claims.evidence: Model badge 'SHARP AR-M207' readable in photo 0 and photo 2. The function list is manufacturer marketing, not a condition claim.
No clip of it powering on, copying or printing; priced as not working.

risks.risk: Copier does not power on or throws error codes.
risks.proof: Clip of the unit switched on, display showing ready, with a handwritten code and date in shot.

risks.risk: Worn drum or fuser giving streaky or faded copies.
risks.proof: Clip making a copy and holding the printed page up to the camera.
risks.if_unproven: as needing drum and fuser replacement

risks.risk: Very high page count shortening remaining life.
risks.proof: Photo of the counter readout or printed counter report.

risks.risk: Missing or damaged internal parts, toner cartridge or cassette parts.
risks.proof: Photo with front door open showing toner and drum unit, and both cassettes pulled out.

proof_requests: Clip of the copier powering on and producing a copy, with a handwritten code and today's date in shot.
Photo of the front door open showing toner and drum, and both paper cassettes pulled out.
One unwrapped photo of the full machine from front and side.
response.reason: The model Sharp AR-M207 is readable on the front badge in photos 0 and 2, so it can be priced at its worst case as a not working unit. A copy test clip and counter photo would raise it.
